newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Renong profit leap fails to excite.
newsitem.headline: Renong profit leap fails to excite.

text.p: Malaysian conglomerate Renong Bhd's near doubling in annual earnings failed to excite most industry analysts despite beating market forecasts, analysts said on Friday.

Much of the profit surge reflected the sale of land in southern Johor state, the analysts said, adding that Renong's cash position remained weak and net profit would have run within expectations if proceeds from the land sale were excluded.

The infrastructure developer announced after the market closed on Thursday a net profit of 407.11 million ringgit for the financial year to June 30, 1996, against 207.83 million ringgit in the previous year.
Analysts had forecast net profit of between 360 million to 390 million ringgit.
Earnings per share rose to 23.6 cents from 12.6 cents.

"The 23.6 cents was some 40 percent above the consensus estimate of 16.9 cents," said Jupiter Securities in a morning report on Friday. "Its excellent results could inject a new lease of life into other main Board companies," it said.
But other analysts were not as enthusiastic.
"The profit numbers are good, but much of the gains are from the proceeds of the sale of land in Johore," said an analyst at a foreign brokerage.
Earlier in the year, Renong sold about 1,060 hectares of land in Johor to companies involved in the construction of the second causeway link to Singapore. The proceeds were about 270 million ringgit.
Renong's 64 percent subsidiary, Prolink Development Sdn Bhd, is the developer of the 10,000-hectare site in Johor.
"The profits are not really representative of the group's cash situation," said the foreign brokerage analyst.
"Their real cash earnings are a lot less than the profit figures suggest," he said. "Around 70 percent of the cash proceeds (from the land sale) will not be collected until three years from now."
Ami Moris, vice-president of dealing at Capitalcorp Securities said: "Renong also has a considerable debt situation, amounting to roughly 17 billion ringgit."
The interest payments on this are going to begin to eat heavily into Renong's long-term earnings prospects, she said.
Most analysts contacted by Reuters said if proceeds of the land sale were factored out of the profit figures, operationally the group performed within their expectations.
HLG Securities said in a commentary: "Revenue and profit jumped due to aggressive recognition of Prolink land sales. Most other associate and subsidiary income was as expected."
Renong subsidiary United Engineers (M) Bhd performed within expectations at the half-year mark, HLG said.

HLG Securities said they are recommending a long-term buy on Renong stock. "Our reluctance to call an outright buy stems from uncertainty over the management's focus on Renong, as interest has shifted somewhat to Intria Bhd," the report said.

Speculation has been rife in the market that Halim Saad, executive chairman and a substantial shareholder of Renong, may also control Intria Bhd and be gradually shifting his attention to the infrastructure developer.
At Friday midday, Renong's shares were up two cents at 3.88, after reaching an intraday high of 3.98 ringgit.
